status_vocabulary.DONE: built as the board draws it; evidence cites the code
status_vocabulary.BUG: wrong or dishonest output today; failure_scenario says how
status_vocabulary.GAP: board element missing; no owner decision needed; size S/M/L

status_vocabulary.OWNER: needs an owner decision (policy, schema, or spec vs settled evidence)

boards.title: Browse
boards.spec_label: No carousel: featured fandoms wrap as a chip cluster in a category-tinted panel with a dashed '+N more' carrying the real remainder. Jump Back In keeps three cards. Needs featured subset + total per category, and FandomDisplayName splitting.

items.what: One full-width panel per category, category hue, wrapping chip cluster, dashed '+N more' with the exact remainder
Featured fandoms
items.note: Shows the twelve largest fandoms from the cached full list instead of AO3's hand-curated featured subset; reasoning in the doc comment (no new request).

items.what: Chips split title / qualifier (FandomDisplayName)
Category work total marked '~' when it is a sum of tag counts
Jump Back In: three cards sized to the width
Jump Back In picks the fandoms you read most recently
items.failure_scenario: The section's doc says 'the fandoms you were most recently reading'. readWorks is sorted by dateAdded, not lastReadDate, and the three slots are filled in category order: a reader who added an anime work a year ago and read a TV work last night sees the anime fandom first, and never the TV one if Anime & Manga has three read fandoms. statsToken ignores reading, so it would not refresh on a read either.
items.fix: Carry lastReadDate (fallback dateAdded) in LibraryWorkSnapshot; sort readWorks by it; build Jump Back In from one global recency-ordered pass (first three distinct fandoms, each mapped to its category) instead of flattening per-category lists; add the newest lastReadDate to statsToken.
items.test: Pure: two works, older-added but newer-read in category B -> B's fandom comes first.

items.what: Jump Back In card's work count
items.note: The count is looked up only among the top-12 cluster chips, case-sensitively, so most cards show no count although the full list (with counts) is cached.
items.fix: Look the fandom up in the category's full catalog list, case-insensitively.

boards.title: Category filter sheet
boards.spec_label: Minimum works, three tag-kind switches with the count each would remove, Favourited only, I have downloads from, Only fandoms with more than one tag; 'Show N tags' button.

items.what: Every row the board draws, with its count, and 'Show N tags'
'I have downloads from' means works you have downloaded
items.failure_scenario: The switch keeps fandoms of works with isSaved (the 'keep permanently' flag). Library's Downloaded shelf means hasEPUB (file on disk). A reader with an unkept, in-progress work in fandom X sees X under Library > Downloaded but not under 'I have downloads from'.
items.fix: Use work.hasEPUB && !work.isQueueOnlyWork, the Downloaded shelf's own rule (or reuse LibrarySectionKind.downloaded's predicate).
items.test: FandomLibraryIndex built from one hasEPUB-but-not-isSaved work lists its fandom under downloads.

boards.title: Work Detail
boards.spec_label: AO3 account actions in their own lane under the summary (Kudos filled); everything local behind one My copy button into a sheet built from the page's parts.

items.what: ON AO3 lane: Kudos (filled when given), Subscribe, Bookmark, Mark for Later
Identity block, figure strip, serif summary, tag clusters, facts card, tally strip, Mark finished, My copy row and sheet
items.note: Element-by-element audit recorded 2026-09-14; spot-checked here (tally strip, kudos lane).

items.what: 'Part 2 of 4' and '9 pages left'
items.note: Deliberately not drawn: neither figure is on the work page; recorded with reasons.

items.what: Sheet ACTIVITY 'Progress Ch 3 - 38%'
items.note: Reads readingProgressLabel, which prints a spine-derived 'Ch N' when the legacy reader wrote lastSpineIndex; same root and fix as home-library 1b.12. The board's combined 'Ch 3 - 38%' can come from WorkReadingPosition.title + readiumProgress.

items.what: Kudos/comments/bookmarks figures prefer the stored local value
items.note: When a local copy exists, its stored figure (from the last refresh) wins over the remote summary that may have just been fetched; a local 0 falls through to the remote. Not false, but can be older than a figure the screen already holds.
items.fix: Prefer the remote summary's figure when present (it is the fresher fetch); fall back to the stored one.

boards.title: Comment composer
boards.spec_label: Medium detent over 1f; Cancel and Post in the header; quoted parent in the rail colour; identity and a 10,000 character budget under the field; footer says the sheet drags taller.

items.what: Medium/large detents, Cancel and Post in the header, quoted parent, identity row
Character budget matches what AO3 counts
items.failure_scenario: The budget subtracts composerText.count (grapheme clusters). AO3 validates the raw comment_content with Rails validates_length_of, which counts Ruby characters (code points), before any sanitizing. A comment of 9,995 graphemes containing a few multi-code-point emoji shows '5 left' and AO3 rejects it as too long.
